metadata.notes: DeepSeek Harness 0.1.5-rc.2 turns quota exhaustion into a terminal model error and immediately permits a later prompt; it has no quota-reset hold that satisfies this scenario.

assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: no
daemon_capability: n/a
driver_capability: ready

## Reasoning

The scenario requires a quota or cost cap to end the active turn, leave the session in `ready`, and prevent later prompts from starting a new turn until the budget resets. DeepSeek Harness 0.1.5-rc.2 does not implement that behavior. Its provider layer distinguishes permanent `QUOTA` failures from transient `RATE_LIMIT` failures. The default retry policy retries `RATE_LIMIT` five times, but does not include `QUOTA` in its retryable codes. When recovery is absent or exhausted, the agent loop throws the model failure and appends a durable `turn/end` with `reason.kind=error`.

The error does not install a quota-reset hold. The agent loop catches the failed driver boundary, returns the agent to its internal idle phase, and `followup()` always inserts the later user message into the next-turn inbox and calls `wakeDriver()`. `wakeDriver()` immediately starts a new running phase and the next `turn()` appends another `turn/start`. A later prompt therefore starts a new turn and another provider request. The Harness can report a quota error, but it cannot keep later prompts idle until reset. That missing gate is fundamental to the scenario, so the agent verdict is `no`, not `partial`.

The required installed-binary scan supports the same result. `strings $(which dsh) | grep -iE 'quota|budget|rate.?limit|429|max.?tokens|cost.?limit'` returned no matches in the 0.1.5-rc.2 launcher. The installed official package documentation and implementation contain provider retry and per-request output-limit surfaces, but no session token/cost budget or quota-reset gate.

Daemon capability is not applicable because the agent does not perform the required lifecycle. For context only, the current DSH parser would map the emitted error `turn/end` to `turn_done` plus a terminal `SessionError`, which classifies as `error`, not the required `ready` hold. That is correct handling of the trace that DSH writes and is not a daemon bug.

The driver is ready by the frozen-no-feature convention. Static inspection reports support for `send`, `wait_turn`, `sleep`, and every other current interactive primitive. No recipe can elicit the missing quota-reset hold, so the recipe is `applicable:false`.

## What would change the verdict

DeepSeek Harness must add a session-level token or cost cap, or a provider-quota latch, that refuses later prompts until a reset condition and persists an observable non-error turn boundary. A later assessment can then judge the daemon and author a driven lifecycle spec.
caveats: Vacuous-pass condition: a meta-only spec passes without producing a quota event. This cell is frozen and makes no behavioral pass claim; adding ordinary working/ready phases would only prove a normal turn.

The Harness does detect provider QUOTA and RATE_LIMIT failures. Detection alone does not satisfy the scenario because the agent records a terminal error and lets the next prompt start another turn immediately.
No live 429 recording was run during assessment. The verdict rests on the installed 0.1.5-rc.2 provider, retry, and agent-loop implementations. Re-probe those sources after an upgrade.
If the agent later adds a persistent quota gate, re-assess daemon capability. The current parser maps error turn boundaries to the canonical error state and does not model a ready quota hold.

sources.note: Installed 0.1.5-rc.2 launcher. The required strings scan for quota, budget, rate limit, 429, max tokens, and cost limit returned no matches.
httpErrorCode classifies provider quota details as QUOTA and other HTTP 429 responses as RATE_LIMIT; non-2xx failures become LlmError values with the normalized code.
The default normal retry policy permits five retries for EMPTY_RESPONSE, RATE_LIMIT, SERVER, TIMEOUT, and TRANSPORT. QUOTA is not retryable.
Official installed package reference: rate limits use bounded normal-mode recovery; an unhandled or exhausted failure leaves retry recovery and remains a model-request failure.

Unhandled model failure is written as turn/end reason.kind=error. The driver then becomes idle; followup inserts a next-turn message and wakeDriver immediately opens another running phase and turn/start. There is no quota-reset latch.
parseTurnEnd maps reason.kind=error to turn_done plus a terminal SessionError. This correctly yields error rather than the scenario's required ready hold.
The static driver scan reports send, wait_turn, sleep, and all other current interactive primitives; no driver primitive can create the missing agent behavior.

recipe.notes: Frozen on agent_supports=no. DeepSeek Harness maps provider quota to an error turn/end and immediately accepts a later prompt as a new turn. It has no persistent quota-reset gate, so no executable recipe can satisfy the required ready hold.
